extracted.intended_audience: Graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and other scientists (and their mentors/administrators) preparing or administering NIH individual fellowship (F-series) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, locating, and understanding NIH Individual (F-series) fellowship opportunities, eligibility by career stage, funding components, and where reviewers' criteria are specified. Applies to applicants at predoctoral, postdoctoral/residency, and established investigator stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Individual Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fellowship programs provide mentored research experience to students and scientists at various stages of their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing an application, emphasize the mentored research and training plan appropriate to the applicant's career stage. The fellowships are intended to provide research experience and training that advance the applicant's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding components (stipend, institutional allowance, tuition/fees, childcare)
rubrics_metrics.description: These fellowships may provide a stipend, institutional allowance to help support the costs of training, tuition and fees, and childcare costs. Please see the funding opportunity for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact stipend levels, institutional allowances, tuition coverage, and childcare support vary by funding opportunity and Institute/Center; applicants must consult the specific FOA/announcement for allowable costs and amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / Predominant mechanism: NRSA
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of NIH-funded fellowships are through the Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award (NRSA) program. Some NIH Institutes and Centers (ICs) may also participate in non-NRSA individual fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should determine whether a given fellowship opportunity is an NRSA (with its specific policies and stipend rules) or a non-NRSA fellowship administered by an IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the criteria reviewers will use to evaluate your application, see Section V of your funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent Announcements include the minimum standard review criteria appropriate for their program. Always consult Section V of the specific FOA or the Parent Announcement to know the exact review criteria and scoring guidance that will be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility & program matching by career stage — Predoctoral
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral: Period during which a student who has earned a bachelor's or equivalent degree is pursuing additional education and performing research to obtain a research doctorate. Clinical students acquire the knowledge to earn the clinical doctorate degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select predoctoral F-series opportunities (e.g., F30, F31) when your current status and training goals match this definition; follow the FOA eligibility details for degree status and institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility & program matching by career stage — Postdoctoral/Residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral refers to a temporary and defined period of mentored advanced training for those who have received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue their chosen career path. Residency refers to a graduate medical education (GME) program that provides physicians with hands-on experience and training in a specific medical specialty after they graduate from medical school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose postdoctoral (e.g., F32) or residency-appropriate fellowship mechanisms depending on your training stage; follow FOA definitions about allowable timing relative to degree conferral and residency status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility & program matching by career stage — Established Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Established Investigator: Stage at which investigator leads research programs in an academic, industry, or government setting with independent (often peer-reviewed) research funding and have delivered significant research outputs due to their experience and scientific quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH offers senior fellowship mechanisms (e.g., F33) for individuals at this stage; ensure your experience and current appointment meet the FOA's definition for 'established.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity codes and example mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of individual fellowship activity codes and mechanisms referenced: Individual Predoctoral NRSA for M.D./Ph.D. Fellowships (F30); Predoctoral Individual NRSA (F31); Predoctoral to Postdoctoral Fellow Transition Award (F99/K00); Ruth L. Kirschstein Postdoctoral Individual NRSA (F32); NRSA for Senior Fellows (F33). Also consider Dissertation Award (R36) and Fellowship for Intramural Dual-Degree Scientists (FIDDS) (FM1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the activity code to identify the correct application forms, eligibility, and review expectations. The page also points applicants to 'View Current Funding Opportunities' and to use Explore NIH Grant Opportunities to search Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative supplements for training and reentry
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative supplement is a non-competing award that provides additional funding to a currently funded grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH participates in programs for full or part-time mentored research training experiences for individuals with high potential to reenter, reintegrate into, or retrain in an active research career. Consult the specific supplement announcement for eligibility and allowable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow updated policies and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow policy notices and program-specific revisions, e.g., 'Revisions to the NIH Fellowship Application and Review Process (For Due Dates On/After January 25, 2025)' and other listed notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check linked policy notices (NOT-OD-24-129, NOT-OD-24-116, NOT-OD-24-107, NOT-OD-24-084, NOT-OD-23-111, etc.) for changes affecting application content, allowable costs, stipend policies, and review criteria that apply to your due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find and apply to opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Explore NIH Grant Opportunities tool to search Grants.gov and view current funding opportunities; review the Grants Process 'Ready to develop your application? Learn from a step-by-step guide.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NIH grants process guidance and the specific FOA instructions (including Section V review criteria) when preparing and submitting an application. Use institute-specific funding considerations and contacts as needed.
